questions.q: What does the article mainly explain?
options: How retirees can maximize benefits by delaying claims until age 70
Why Social Security filings surged last year after years of later claiming
How the 1983 amendments shifted retirement ages for American workers
Why employers replaced pensions with 401(k) plans and retiree insurance
questions.explain: Claims jumped in reaction to turmoil and negative signals about Social Security.

questions.q: What positive trend had researchers been cheering until recently?
options: Older Americans were staying in the labor force longer and delaying claims
Employers were restoring pensions and retiree health benefits for many workers
The Social Security trust fund was growing and reducing doubts about benefits
Young workers were entering the workforce in unusually large numbers
questions.explain: Researchers had noted that older Americans were working and claiming later, improving retirement outlooks.

questions.q: What signals from the Trump administration contributed to the surge in claims?
options: Announcements of extra funding, added staff, and expanded field office hours
Calls to expand payroll taxes and increase benefits for all retirees
False claims of widespread fraud, staff cuts, and threatened field office closures
Neutral technical reports about demographic trends and long-term financing shortfalls
questions.explain: The article cites false fraud claims, thousands of staff cuts and threats to close field offices as negative signals that prompted the surge.

questions.q: What happened to claiming levels from October 2025 to April 2026?
options: They remained at the earlier elevated level and did not drop
They fell by about the same amount as the earlier surge, essentially reversing it
They increased again after a small dip and stayed higher
They fell slightly but left a net gain compared with normal years
questions.explain: New claims fell by about 235,000 (roughly a 10 percent drop), effectively canceling the prior surge.

questions.q: What does the 2021 Boston College headline study imply about the 2025 surge?
options: Fear-inducing news can push people to claim earlier
Neutral headlines caused people to delay claiming by years
Few readers notice headlines about Social Security
Younger people respond most to headlines
questions.explain: Scarier headlines led people to say they would claim about a year earlier, matching the 2025 coverage.
